LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines sources for two architectures (x86_64 and aarch64), both pointing to prebuilt release binaries hosted on GitHub under the project's own repository. The URLs are constructed using the declared `url` variable and the `pkgver` version, which is a standard and safe practice. The `sha256sums` are provided and not set to 'SKIP', indicating verified downloads. There is no `pkgver()` function, so no dynamic version calculation occurs at sourcing time. The top-level scope contains only static declarations and no command substitutions or immediate executions.

Fetching the sources via `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will download the prebuilt tarballs from the project's official GitHub releases, which is expected behavior. The `--printsrcinfo` command will only parse these static declarations and does not execute any build or prepare functions. No network requests outside the declared sources or data exfiltration mechanisms are present in the global scope or `pkgver()` (which is absent). Therefore, running these commands is safe.

As per the guidelines, even if checksums were 'SKIP', that alone would not make this unsafe for this gate. Here, however, checksums are provided and valid. All operations during sourcing are limited to standard package metadata evaluation and source fetching from trusted upstream locations.
</details>

The sources point to prebuilt binaries hosted on the official GitHub repository of the project (https://github.com/a77ila/pactience), specifically from the release page for version v0.2.3. There are no executable commands, scripts, or network operations embedded in this file. It does not contain any obfuscated content, suspicious URLs, or unauthorized data exfiltration mechanisms. The use of prebuilt binaries (`-bin` package) is common in AUR for software written in languages like Rust or Go, where reproducible builds may be complex. While using prebuilt binaries inherently requires trust in the builder, the source URLs are transparent and verifiable, and the checksums match official releases.

This file adheres to standard AUR packaging practices and shows no signs of tampering or malicious intent.
